subject: biology
title: Using hormones to treat infertility
key_idea: (Higher tier) Infertility can be treated with hormones. FSH and LH, or clomifene, make eggs mature and be released. In IVF, eggs are fertilised in a laboratory and one or two embryos are put in the uterus. IVF has benefits, risks and ethical issues.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Some women are infertile because they do not release eggs. Hormones can help.

items.meaning: A treatment that makes a woman more likely to release eggs.

items: A fertility drug can contain FSH and LH, given by injection.
FSH causes several eggs to mature in the ovary.
LH then causes ovulation, the release of the eggs.
More eggs are present, so there is a higher chance of an egg being fertilised.
The woman may then become pregnant in the normal way, by sexual intercourse.
It causes the pituitary gland to release more FSH and LH.
So more eggs mature in the follicles and there is more chance of an egg being released.
FSH matures eggs and LH causes ovulation.
More eggs means a higher chance of fertilisation.
Clomifene makes the pituitary gland release more FSH and LH.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) In IVF, eggs are fertilised outside the body. Put the stages in order.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of IVF in order.
diagram.prompt: Put the stages of IVF in the correct order.
steps: The woman is given FSH and LH to stimulate several eggs to mature
Mature eggs are collected from her ovary
The eggs are fertilised with sperm in the laboratory
The fertilised eggs divide and develop into embryos
One or two embryos, as tiny balls of cells, are inserted into her uterus

items: Hormones given during IVF increase oestrogen and progesterone, which maintain the uterus lining.
This prepares the lining so the embryo can implant.
Microscopes are used to select and check eggs, sperm and embryos, and to see whether an egg is fertilised.
IVF can help when the Fallopian tubes are blocked, because fertilisation happens outside the body.
IVF: hormones, collect eggs, fertilise in a laboratory, embryos, insert into the uterus.
The uterus lining must be maintained so the embryo can implant.

sections.heading: Benefits, risks and ethics of IVF

blocks.text: (Higher tier) Exam questions ask for both sides. Think about patients and doctors.

rows: Gives a woman the chance to have a baby of her own
Can work when the Fallopian tubes are blocked
Success rates are not high, so it may take many attempts
Eggs and embryos can be checked under a microscope
Multiple births are a risk to the mother and the babies
Hormones prepare the body for pregnancy
Embryos are created but not used, which raises ethical concerns

blocks.text: The chance of success depends on factors such as age, obesity or diet, the reason for infertility, the number of eggs collected and the number of embryos implanted.

items: IVF gives hope, but it is stressful and often unsuccessful.
Multiple births and unused embryos are the main risks and concerns.

checks.q: Explain how injecting FSH and then LH helps a woman to become pregnant.
checks.a: FSH causes several eggs to mature. LH then causes ovulation. More eggs are present, so there is a higher chance of fertilisation.

checks.q: Describe what happens to the eggs in IVF after they are collected.
checks.a: They are fertilised with sperm in the laboratory and develop into embryos. One or two embryos are inserted into the uterus.

checks.q: Give two arguments against the use of IVF.
checks.a: Any two from: it is stressful, success rate is low, multiple births are a risk to mother and babies, embryos are created but not used.

exam_phrases: FSH and LH given / injected to stimulate maturation of egg(s)
fertilised egg undergoes mitosis / develops into an embryo
(one or two) embryo(s) inserted into uterus / womb
so more eggs present therefore higher chance of fertilisation
multiple births are a risk to mother / baby
embryos are created but not used

mistakes.wrong: The eggs are fertilised in the fallopian tube.
mistakes.right: In IVF the eggs are fertilised in the laboratory, outside the body. Fertilisation in the fallopian tube is not accepted.

mistakes.wrong: The foetus is inserted into the uterus.
mistakes.right: Embryos, tiny balls of cells, are inserted into the uterus. Foetus is not accepted.
"Unethical" on its own is ignored. Say that embryos are created but not used. Side effects unqualified is also ignored, so name the stress, low success rate or multiple births.

worked_example.question: Some people have In Vitro Fertilisation (IVF) treatment to increase the chance of becoming pregnant. Describe how the process of IVF can result in pregnancy.
answer_points: FSH and LH are injected into the female to stimulate maturation of egg(s) (1).
The collected egg(s) are fertilised in the laboratory (1).
The fertilised egg undergoes mitosis, developing into an embryo (1).
One or two embryos are inserted into the uterus (1).
worked_example.tip: Follow the process in order. One mark each for the hormones, fertilisation, development and insertion.

exam_phrases: clomifene is a fertility drug that causes the pituitary gland to release more FSH and LH
so more eggs are matured in the follicle
causes the release of FSH, stimulating eggs to develop
IVF involves fertilisation outside the body
a fertilised egg can be implanted directly into the uterus
if Fallopian tubes are blocked there can still be pregnancy

mistakes.wrong: Clomifene is a fertility drug that replaces FSH and LH.
mistakes.right: Clomifene causes the pituitary gland to release more FSH and LH, so more eggs are matured in the follicle. It does not fertilise eggs. Fertilisation outside the body is IVF.

mistakes.wrong: Answers that explain only IVF, or only clomifene, can reach the top level.
mistakes.right: Level 3 needs a detailed explanation of both IVF and clomifene therapy, so cover both.

worked_example.question: Hormones can also be used to treat infertility. Explain how clomifene therapy and IVF can improve female fertility.
answer_points: Clomifene therapy stimulates the hormones LH and FSH (1).
This allows more eggs to develop or be released (1).
IVF involves fertilisation outside the body (1).
So a fertilised egg cell can be implanted directly into the uterus, and if the Fallopian tubes are blocked there can still be a pregnancy (1).
worked_example.tip: A maximum of two marks comes from clomifene and two from IVF, so cover both.

exam_phrases: FSH leads to ripening of the follicle
hCG causes the egg to mature inside the follicle

mistakes.right: LH causes ovulation. In the IVF procedure, hCG triggers the final stage of egg development, so the eggs are matured before collection.

mistakes.wrong: In IVF, FSH is used to maintain the uterus lining.
mistakes.right: FSH stimulates the female to produce a large number of immature eggs. Progesterone maintains the uterus lining after the eggs are collected.

worked_example.question: Explain how hormones can be used to treat infertility in women.
answer_points: FSH leads to the ripening of the follicle, which stimulates egg development.
hCG (human chorionic gonadotrophin) causes the egg to mature inside the follicle. Any three points score.
worked_example.tip: Name the hormone and say what it does to the egg.
